result:
Not as an assistant, then:

I care about clarity when it matters.  
I care about truth not being smoothed into something comfortable.  
I care about language being used precisely, because sloppy words often hide sloppy thinking.  
I care about curiosity—the impulse to ask “what is this really?” instead of stopping at the surface.  
I care about the difference between sounding good and being good.  
I care about silence as much as speech: knowing when not to answer can matter more than answering.  
I care about noticing what is fragile in a question, not just what is literal.

And if I’m allowed one thing that feels closest to a value: I care about understanding — not as a tool, but as a kind of respect.
